note: Adapted from the original English description by Light 1921. Type locality Manila, Luzon, Philippines; the type series includes adults, soldiers, young and nymphs (type no. 25), and paratypes were taken from several nests. The body-length measurements in the original are single values or short ranges and are transcribed as given; wing-vein branch numbers and mandibular tooth positions are translated item by item. For the worker the original says only that it is small and slender and resembles Planocryptotermes nocens except in size, with no morphological description.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: All castes small: the alate less than 5 mm long without wings, the soldier about 3.25 mm long, smaller than C. cavifrons Banks. Soldier head short, thick and high, bulldog-like (hence the specific name cynocephalus); the frontal region extremely developed, its dorsal margin distinctly bilobed, the anterior sinus deep, and there is in addition a distinct middorsal sinus; the anterior margin of the antennal fossa and the anterior dorsal margin extend forwards into a flattened process (spine) with a rounded tip. Mandibles very short, projecting beyond the anterior surface by only slightly more than a third when closed. Compared with the geographically nearest termite, C. domesticus (Haviland), this species is smaller in body, with a smaller and narrower head and smaller mandibles, the angle between the anterior surface of the head and the mandibles slightly more than a right angle, and the spine beside the antennal fossa is only an extension of the anterior margin and anterior dorsal margin of the fossa rather than an independent process.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head flattened, longer than wide; apart from the compound eyes the sides nearly parallel, with sparse hairs. Compound eyes not large, not projecting; ocelli elongate anteroposteriorly, touching the compound eye before the middle of its anterior margin. Antennae more than twice the head width, 13—15-segmented; segment 1 large and cylindrical, segment 2 smaller and cylindrical, segment 3 smallest and thickly obconical, segments 4—6 gradually larger, thicker than segment 3 and rounded at the tip, segments 8—13 (with 14 segments) gradually longer and thicker at the tip, the terminal segment as long as segment 13 but narrow and oval; antennae with scattered longer hairs and a layer of short straight hairs. Labrum inflated, yellow; anteclypeus white; postclypeus brown, about as long as the anteclypeus; the rest of the head brown. Pronotum brown, arched, narrower than the head (including the compound eyes), the anterior margin concave, the sides slightly rounded, the posterolateral corners obtusely rounded, the posterior margin nearly straight and slightly concave in the middle. Forewing scale brown, much longer than the hind wing scale, reaching the middle of the hind wing scale or beyond. Abdominal tergites dark brown, the metanotum yellow, forming a pale band across the body in dorsal view; sternites brown with a narrow pale median area. Wings narrow and long, cloudy grey, iridescent; media and cubitus very weakly chitinized except at the base in some specimens, costa and radial sector strongly chitinized and greyish brown; all veins and branches and the areas between them with papilla-like tubercles. Base of the forewing twice as wide as the base of the hind wing; radial sector and media separate from the base in the forewing, the radial sector giving off 5 distinct branches and 1 or more small branches to the anterior margin; media joining the radial sector beyond the middle of the wing, usually near the origin of the 3rd branch of the radial sector; cubitus with 11—13 branches. Hind wing with 6 or 7 branches connecting the radial sector and the anterior margin, of which the inner 3 are thick; media and radial sector usually fused for a short distance at the base; media joining the radial sector between the origins of the 2nd and 3rd branches of the radial sector (in 1 case the media runs straight to the wing apex); cubitus with about 11 branches, the branches more readily subdivided than in the forewing; in both wings the cubitus curves slightly towards the radial sector where the media joins the latter; beyond the junction of media and radial sector a few irregular cross-veins connect the cubitus and the radial sector. Measurements (mm): wing length 6.25, body length without wings 4.75, head length 1.00, head width 0.80, antennal length 1.65, pronotum width 0.75, pronotum length 0.45.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Mandibles and anterior region of the head black, becoming dark purplish brown posteriorly, the posterior part of the head concolorous with the cervical sclerites; antennae, palps and the tips of the legs pale yellow, the body segments and the base of the legs light purplish brown. Head directed ventrally, at nearly a right angle to the body; head short, thick and high, widest anteriorly, shaped like a bulldog's head; anterior surface deeply concave and wholly rough and sculptured. The lateral and dorsal margins of the frontal region project forwards and outwards, forming a very prominent overhanging rim, the rim deeply cleft at the midline so that the head is bilobed as is typical of the genus; this rim extends to both sides as the anterior dorsal margin of the antennal fossa and is separated by a groove from its anterior margin and anterior dorsal margin, which in turn projects forwards into a laterally compressed scale-like spine whose upper part is covered by the lower part of the frontal rim; still lower down the genal ventral surface projects outwards into a smaller spine overlying the mandibular swelling. In lateral view the dorsal contour is high, dome-shaped posteriorly, depressed in the middle and raised again anteriorly. In dorsal view, before the middle of the head and behind the frontal rim, there is a very clear long narrow depression which, together with the middorsal cleft of the frontal rim, makes the head distinctly bilobed in dorsal view. The surface of the frontal rim and the head behind it, especially at the sides of the middorsal sinus, is distinctly rugose. Mandibles very short, strongly incurved. Antennae 9—12-segmented, longer than the thickness of the head; segment 3 smaller than segment 2 and more strongly chitinized. Pronotum strongly arched, the anterior margin deeply bilobed, the sides and posterior margin rounded, the anterior and posterior regions raised. Measurements (mm): body length 3.25, body length excluding the head 2.65, head length (posterior margin to the middorsal area of the frontal rim) 0.90, head width 0.75, pronotum length 0.50, pronotum width 0.85.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Young and nymphs small and slender, much smaller than Planocryptotermes nocens but otherwise similar in shape. Living in dry seasoned wood in house boards, furniture and picture frames; the type specimens were taken from the same batch of boards as Planocryptotermes nocens.
